The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f859efa28f227ff), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 15-16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Take nested frequency grids at scales K < K′, rounded within fixed factors. Assemble all child fields in each parent cap, and localize them on its parent physical grid. The localizers can be chosen band-limited, with summable Schwartz tails and bounded sums, so that the resulting parent packets have amplitudes aT and satisfy b2 T ≥ c X T′ in the parent cap b2 T′ wT′ (zT ) (2.23) whenever the parent weights are chosen to dominate the displayed sum. For 2 < p ≤ qk, X T Kk+2 ap T b2−p T ≤ Cε(K′ /K)ε X T′ (K′ )k+2 ap T′ b2−p T′ . (2.24) 15 It remains valid after retaining any subset of parent cells, at every step of a finite hierarchy. After modifying a child field, use its fresh amplitudes in the same fixed parent masks. On subtrees lying in a codimension-one strip at their final frequency resolution one may use p = qk−1 at every transition; for k = 1 any fixed finite p > 2 is available. Products of the transition estimates give the complete finite-hierarchy estimate. Fixed polynomial weights on macroscopic boxes, and any fixed additional edge decay, are allowed. Their orders are chosen once, before the finite grid is chosen. Constants may depend on the finite grid; the required original profile regularity and decay order do not grow with its depth.
